source.title: MMATR-X: High-Resolution Optical-SAR Joint Pretraining via Conditioned Alignment and Degraded-Target Prediction
source.authors: Bowen Peng; Yongxiang Liu; Jie Zhou; Xiaodong Chen; Tianpeng Liu; Xiaogang Yu; Li Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, but Figures 8 and 10 are represented only by captions and textual descriptions; their plotted values are not available.
record.tranche_reason: The paper argues for and reports pair-dependent, incomplete cross-modal alignment rather than scale-driven convergence across independently trained models. Its own representation-similarity results show that the relationship varies with local correspondence and training objective.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s measurements of raw optical-SAR embedding cosine similarity across patch-level SSIM bins (Fig. 10) and its qualitative UMAP geometry comparison (Fig. 8). Fig. 1 measures input-image SSIM, not learned representations; the singular-value spectra in Fig. 7 describe within-representation geometry, not cross-modal alignment. Downstream task scores and ablation scores are not representation-similarity results. Fig. 10 gives qualitative trends in the text but no readable plotted values.
record.test_reason: This is an optical-SAR pretraining method paper, so it does not test the claim. Its similarity and UMAP results compare optical and SAR embeddings from one shared encoder. That encoder was trained jointly with objectives built to align the two modalities (contrastive CCL, cross-modal prediction, distillation). The paper therefore induces cross-modal agreement on purpose and does not measure it arising between independently trained models. It never varies scale or capability and does not cite the original sources. Its cosine-versus-SSIM analysis compares the authors' own training variants, not models converging, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that optical-SAR correspondence is partial and pair-dependent. Pair-conditioned alignment (CCL) and degraded-target prediction (CDP) therefore improve transfer while retaining modality-specific variation. Their pretrained model MMATR-X leads on optical, SAR and dual-modal benchmarks, with consistent gains in controlled optical-DEM and RGB-depth experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests a proposed optical-SAR pretraining framework and its representation geometry; it does not reproduce the original sources’ scale-based cross-model similarity measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Raw embedding cosine similarity varies across patch-level SSIM bins, and the reported redistribution differs between CCL and CDP.

fits_no_version.finding: In one shared optical-SAR encoder, the paper's pair-conditioned contrastive (CCL) and degraded-target (CDP) objectives redistribute raw paired-embedding cosine similarity across patch-SSIM bins relative to their direct counterparts. Similarity falls for high-SSIM pairs and rises for low-SSIM pairs; UMAP shows modality separation retained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within jointly trained multimodal encoders, the training objective shapes how strongly paired cross-modal embedding similarity tracks input-level correspondence.

record.problems: The relevant similarity evidence is qualitative in the supplied text and the plotted values are unavailable; the UMAP evidence is a qualitative projection. The study tests one optical-SAR setting and does not compare alternative similarity metrics, scales, or model capability levels.
record.rows_left_out: Fig. 1 input-image SSIM is not a learned-representation measurement. Fig. 7 singular-value spectra concern within-representation geometry. Tables 8-11 and downstream benchmark tables report training ablations or task performance, not cross-modal representation similarity.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models across scale or capability.
No vision-language models or image-caption pairs, and no alignment measured against model quality.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation transfer between separately trained models.
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
No comparison of similarity metrics or their settings applied to convergence between independent models.
No measurement of alignment completeness, plateau or its cause between independent models.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tranche T5 and its V6/V7 support labels are dropped. Nothing in the paper concerns convergence of independently trained models: all similarity is between the two modalities in one jointly trained, alignment-supervised encoder. The rows are comparisons of the authors' own objectives, and every plotted value is figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test alignment rising with model scale or capability across independently trained models of different architectures, objectives, and data.
The study concerns optical-SAR pairs, not vision-language models paired on images and captions, and does not test alignment rising as both models improve.
No comparison across random initializations or shared features across seeds is reported.
The paper does not test mapping one model’s representations onto another’s, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
The paper does not test whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.

It reports cosine similarity across local input-correspondence bins, but does not compare alternative representation-similarity metrics or their settings, neighbour counts, or out-of-distribution inputs.

The paper reports modality separation and correspondence-dependent similarity patterns, but does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared training data/objectives rather than a common model of reality cause alignment.
